details:
Q1: How should the poller's review-blocked judge `fix` path (`rb_fix_scope_check`) treat staged edits under `.github/`, `scripts/`, `prompts/`, `.claude/` and `workflow-templates/`?
Choices:
A) Always reject them, whatever `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS` is set to. A rejected fix uses up one review-blocked retry and sends the existing Telegram warning. Protected repairs then go through the judge's other actions (`merge_with_followup` / `close_and_reissue`), so the normal implement → review pipeline makes them. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Always reject by default, and add a new opt-in repo variable (e.g. `REVIEW_BLOCKED_FIX_ALLOW_PROTECTED_EDITS`, default `false`) that brings back today's behaviour. **Note:** turning the variable on reopens this finding.
C) Build the hunk-level provenance check the issue recommends: staged protected hunks may be pushed only when a trusted fix specification, generated outside the judge, authorizes them. This is much larger and needs a new trusted-spec mechanism designed first.
Q2: Should the fix also cover the standalone review-blocked judge's fix path in `scripts/review_rb_judge.sh`, which has no protected-path check today?
Choices:
A) No. Change only the orchestrator poller path the finding cites (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`), and file any standalone hardening as a separate issue. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Yes. Apply the same protected-path rule to the standalone judge's fix commit in the same PR.
Q3: Besides the poller-side rejection, should the review-blocked judge prompt (`prompts/mode-judge-review-blocked.txt`) be told that protected files can't be edited, so it stops choosing `fix` for those findings?
Choices:
A) Yes. Add a short prompt rule and pass a flag into the poller's judge prompt so the judge picks `merge_with_followup` / `close_and_reissue` straight away instead of using up retries on fixes that will be rejected. (RECOMMENDED)
B) No. Enforce it only on the poller side and leave the prompt as it is.
